1.0.0.en: The strangers: 1- The Jewish converts to Christianity who dwell in the countries of the world and are strangers far from Judea.

1.0.1.en: 2- Believers in general are strangers in the world, because their homeland is heaven.

1.0.2.en: The dispersion: the Jewish converts to Christianity who were scattered because of the Jewish persecution of them in Judea and went to the various countries of the world.

1.0.3.en: Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia: countries located in Asia Minor, which is present-day Turkey.

1.0.4.en: The Apostle Peter addresses his epistle to the Jewish converts to Christianity who were scattered in the countries of Asia Minor, and also to all believers in the world who suffer persecutions because of their Christianity.

1.1.0.en: The foreknowledge of God: God the Father knows who will believe in Him, and this shows His love and care for His children from eternity.

1.1.1.en: Sanctification of the Spirit unto obedience: the Holy Spirit sanctifies believers and consecrates their hearts to obey God's commandments.

1.1.2.en: The sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: the blood of Christ, which saves those who believe in Him from their sins and gives them the heavenly Kingdom. He used the expression "sprinkling of blood," an expression from the Jewish Law, which sprinkled the blood of animals that were a type of the blood of Christ the Redeemer.

1.1.3.en: He sends the love of the Holy Trinity, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, who works in believers and grants them His grace and peace, which the Apostle Peter wishes for them and sends to them.

1.1.4.en: Offer words of encouragement, wishing God's work for those you meet, so that their hearts may rejoice and you may draw them to think about God and to rely on Him.

1.1.5.en: (2) The joys of salvation (vv. 3-8) 3 Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which according to his abundant mercy hath begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, 4 To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you, 5 Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time. 6 Wherein ye greatly rejoice, though now for a season, if need be, ye are in heaviness through manifold temptations: 7 That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ: 8 Whom having not seen, ye love; in whom, though now ye see him not, yet believing, ye rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory:

1.2.0.en: Blessed be God the Father, who by His rich mercy gave us the new birth through Baptism. For man used to be born according to the flesh, under the rule of death, but he who is born according to the Spirit is a son of God and an heir with Christ, with a living hope in eternity, whose pledge is the resurrection of the Lord from the dead.

1.3.0.en: The characteristics of this spiritual inheritance are:

1.3.2.en: (2) Undefiled: it is not defiled by the sins that we left behind through repentance during our life on earth. (3) That fadeth not away: that is, it does not pass away.

1.3.3.en: (4) Reserved in heaven: God guards it for us and awaits us in heaven after we complete our striving on earth.

1.3.4.en: Let us hold fast to faith and hope with joy, and not despair because of present, temporary sufferings.

1.4.0.en: God keeps us in the faith and guards us from the wars of the devil, so that we may complete our striving and attain salvation on the great Day of Judgment.

1.5.0.en: This salvation gladdens your hearts, even though you will face trials and persecutions from the world that will grieve you for a time during your life on earth. But they do not take away your joy and peace, which will be completed in heaven, where all sorrows pass away.

1.6.0.en: He likens faith to gold that is refined by fire, so that its impurities are removed and its brightness appears. In the same way faith is purified of the impurities of weakness and sin through trials, which fire signifies, and so it becomes great (it is remembered), and God praises it on the Day of Judgment and because of it brings us into the glories of heaven.

1.7.0.en: During our life on earth we believe in Christ and love Him, so we endure afflictions for His sake, and our hearts rejoice in fellowship with Him, since we believe in His presence with us. Although we do not see Him with our physical eyes, we feel His work in us, and so we rejoice with a joy that cannot be expressed here on earth, as a pledge of the joys of heaven that we shall receive.

1.8.s.en: (3) Salvation, the goal of the prophets

1.8.0.en: The Apostle directs believers to the fact that their goal in believing in Christ is to receive eternal salvation in the Kingdom of Heaven. We continue to receive this salvation on earth, as he says "receiving," and this takes place in the Church through the Holy Sacraments and the means of grace. The original translation is "the salvation of your souls," not "the salvation of souls."

1.9.0.en: The salvation that Christ accomplished on the cross, and that we receive through the sacraments of the Church, was longed for and sought by the prophets, who prophesied about it in the Old Testament.

1.10.0.en: The Spirit of Christ which was in them: the Holy Spirit.

1.10.1.en: The Holy Spirit revealed to the prophets the life of Christ, His sufferings and His resurrection, but they did not know exactly the time of the fulfillment of this salvation. Even the prophet Daniel, to whom the time was revealed, did not grasp and understand these meanings because of the greatness of this salvation. There are many prophecies about the sufferings of Christ, such as (Isa 53, Dan 9:27), and likewise many prophecies about the resurrection of Christ and His ascension, such as (Ps 16:8-11, Isa 38:11).

1.11.0.en: The prophets understood that their prophecy would be fulfilled after a time and that they would not behold this salvation with their own eyes, but we, who have enjoyed this good news through the Apostles, have received this salvation. The angels also desired to see the fulfillment of this salvation of which they had heard. Thus the prophets were servants of salvation by their prophecies about it, and we received it in the New Testament through the redemption of Christ.

1.11.1.en: May your salvation from sin and your enjoyment of fellowship with Christ be your only goal, so that you are not hindered from it while you carry out your other aims. Rather, give up everything that hinders you, and remind yourself of this at the beginning of every day.

1.12.0.en: Wherefore: because of the importance of this salvation and its glories.

1.12.1.en: Gird up the loins of your mind: keep your thoughts under control, away from all evil, and be strengthened by the word of Christ for striving and pressing on in the way of the Kingdom.

1.12.2.en: Be sober: attentiveness and spiritual vigilance to reject all evil and to seize opportunities for life with God. The grace that is to be brought unto you: the complete salvation that you receive in the Kingdom.

1.12.3.en: At the revelation of Jesus Christ: the Day of Judgment, on which the righteous will be rewarded.

1.12.4.en: The Apostle defines our duties toward this salvation as follows:

1.12.5.en: First: readiness of mind. We must prepare our thoughts and be attentive, with all our senses and abilities, to spiritual striving.

1.12.6.en: Second: hope. We are not troubled by the sufferings of this temporary life, but rely with firm hope on the grace of God, which will grant us salvation in the Kingdom and compensate us for the toils of this life.

1.13.0.en: Third: repentance. Because believers are children of God, they must obey His commandments and repent of their former evil desires, in which they lived when they did not know Him and were far from Him before faith.

1.14.0.en: Fourth: holiness. He calls them to sanctify and consecrate their hearts to God by their good conduct, following the example of the holy Christ, as it is written in (Lev 11:44).

1.15.0.en: Fifth: walking in the fear of God:

1.15.1.en: If God is our tender Father, who redeemed us by His love on the cross, He is also the just Judge who judges our faults. Our attention to God's justice makes us fear Him and feel our estrangement from this perishing world, so we leave our sins, respect His presence with us and please Him in everything.

1.15.2.en: The fear of God protects you from every sin. So remember every day that you will meet God the just Judge, so that you repent, keep away from every evil that defiles you, live in holiness, and be at ease in every step you take.

1.16.0.en: Your vain conversation: your former life, which was far from God. Although it seemed upright, it did not truly qualify them to await Christ.

1.16.1.en: Received by tradition from your fathers: you learned it and acquired it from your Jewish fathers.

1.16.2.en: As of a lamb without blemish: in the Jewish Law, a lamb with no blemishes was offered as a sacrifice, and this was a type of Christ, who is slain for us on the cross.

1.16.3.en: He shows the greatness of the salvation that they receive in the Church, by which they were set free from slavery to sin and from the old life far from God. This was not by paying a material price such as silver and gold, which are perishing material things, but by paying the costliest price, which is the precious blood of Christ, which the blood of the animals offered in the Old Testament signified, and which is more precious and greater than the blood of animals.

1.17.0.en: This salvation was in God's eternal knowledge before He created the world. By His knowledge He knew that man would sin and need redemption, and by His love He was ready for that. The ordinances of the Old Testament were types and pointers to this salvation, which was manifested in the fullness of time by the blood of Christ, who saves everyone in the whole world who believes in Him.

1.18.0.en: By Him ye believe in God: through Christ the Redeemer your faith in God is strengthened and established.

1.18.1.en: The redemption of Christ, which fulfilled all the prophecies, establishes the faith of the Jews, especially after they learned that He rose from the dead and ascended in glory into heaven, so that their hope is fastened on eternity.

1.19.0.en: Since we have this salvation, we are careful to obey the commandments of Christ, which are the truth, and this with the help of the Holy Spirit. Then our hearts are purified from every sin, and we are able to love one another deeply and fervently from the heart.

1.20.0.en: The believer remembers that he has been born again of Christ the Word through the sacrament of Baptism, and not merely by the first, physical birth, which does not remove sin from man and exposes him to eternal torment, whereas the second birth prepares him to receive complete salvation in blessed eternity. He likens the physical birth to a seed that will die, that is, the body will decay in the dust, whereas the second birth is a spiritual seed, that is, it prepares us for the Kingdom of Heaven.

1.21.0.en: He likens the life of man on earth to grass, that is, a plant that lasts a few months and then falls and dries up. So also the life of man, with all its material glories, will end in death, however great the glory may seem, like beautiful flowers: it will wither, fall to the ground and die.

1.22.0.en: The good news which they received is the good news of Christ the Word, who gives us a life that endures forever in heaven.

1.22.1.en: Look at the grace of your knowing Christ and all that you receive from Him in the Church, so that you take care with your prayers in it and repent of your sins, and enjoy the blessings of salvation all the days of your life on earth until it is completed in heaven.

1.22.2.en: Christ the cornerstone and the characteristics of His children

2.0.0.en: Through Baptism we become children of God, and in our new life we must rid ourselves through repentance of all sins, among them:

2.0.3.en: Hypocrisies: showing something other than what is inside.

2.0.5.en: Evil speakings: anger together with abuse.

2.1.0.en: The sincere milk of the word: spiritual food, which includes Holy Communion, the word of God and all spiritual practices.

2.1.1.en: He likens believers who are born again of Baptism to infants who desire to drink pure, unadulterated milk from their mother the Church, that is, they should take care to be nourished by the Holy Sacraments, the Holy Bible, sermons, prayer and all spiritual things, so that they may continue in their spiritual growth.

2.2.0.en: If so be: since you have. "If" here expresses certainty, not doubt.

2.2.1.en: Because you have tasted the milk of the Church, the Mother, and have experienced the sweetness of fellowship with the good and tender Lord, to whom you draw near through prayers, worship and partaking of the Holy Sacraments, you will behold Him as a living stone on which your whole life rests. The likening of Christ to a stone is to affirm that He is the foundation of the spiritual building of every believer in Him, and He is a living stone because He is the living God and the giver of life to those who believe in Him.

2.2.2.en: The chief priests of the Jews rejected Christ and killed Him, relying on the greatness of their temple and their worship, all of which signify Him. But Christ is the only Son, chosen by God for the redemption of mankind, and He is the most precious and greatest of men; He is the example of the perfect man whom we ought to follow.

2.2.3.en: The Holy Bible has symbolized Christ by the stone in the rock that gave water in the wilderness to the children of Israel (Ex 17:6), by the stone cut out without hands as the prophet Daniel said (Dan 2:45), and by the stone of help that Samuel set up (1 Sam 7:12).

2.2.4.en: Do not be troubled if people reject your words and accuse you of what is not in you, so long as you hold fast to God's commandments. Seek His help, stand firm in your faith with meekness and gentleness, and be confident that God will in the end reveal your righteousness.

2.3.0.en: If Christ has been likened to the living stone to whom we come by faith and holy worship, the Apostle asks them to be:

2.3.1.en: Lively stones: that is, steadfast and firmly rooted in faith in Him, so that we live by His life.

2.3.2.en: A spiritual house: we all become members of one body, which is the Church, and it includes the saints in heaven, who are the triumphant Church, and the believers striving on earth, who are the militant Church; all are one house. The life of every believer becomes a spiritual house in which God dwells and works by His Holy Spirit to offer worship and good works.

2.3.3.en: A holy priesthood: every believer offers his body and his life as a sacrifice of love to God, through prayers, praise and works of goodness, and this is the general priesthood. Likewise the priests lead the Church in offering the Holy Sacraments before God, and this is the special priesthood.

2.3.4.en: Spiritual sacrifices: such as humility, repentance from sins, the rejection of selfishness, striving in worship, labor in service, and thanksgiving at all times.

2.3.5.en: By Jesus Christ: all the striving of life rests on the salvation that Christ the Redeemer gives us.

2.4.0.en: In the Old Testament God declared through the mouth of His prophets (Isa 28:16) that from the Jews would come Christ, the Savior of the world, whom He likens to a chief cornerstone, that is, the stone that joins two perpendicular walls. He is the foundation of the building, chosen by God for the redemption of mankind, and precious because He is the only-begotten Son, and whoever believes in Him is saved. When he lives his whole life in Him, he triumphs over the devil and is not put to shame in eternity, but enjoys the Kingdom.

2.5.0.en: Everyone who believes in Christ and lives by faith until the end of his life receives inexpressible honor and glory in heaven. As for those who refuse to believe in Christ, they will discover on the last day that He is the foundation of salvation, and eternal torment awaits all who rejected Him. Christ said this about Himself in (Lk 20:17).

2.6.0.en: A stone of stumbling and a rock of offence: Isaiah prophesied this about Christ (Isa 8:14). He is a shock to the sensual, since He deprives them of their evil pleasures, and an offence to the proud among the Jews, who hoped for Him to be an earthly king who would save them from the Romans, and likewise to the proud in the world, such as the Greeks, who wanted Him to be great on earth and not crucified and weak in outward appearance.

2.6.1.en: Being disobedient to the word: those who refuse faith do not obey the commandments of Christ.

2.6.2.en: Whereunto also they were appointed: in God's eternal knowledge He knows that they will refuse faith and receive eternal torment, even though these Jews ought to have been the people of God and the first to believe in Him. The Apostle makes clear that for unbelievers the Gospel of Christ will be against their lusts and earthly thoughts, so they do not obey it, and consequently it will condemn them on the last day and they will be cast into the eternal fire.

2.7.0.en: After speaking of those who reject faith, he speaks to the believers and gives them the following titles:

2.7.1.en: A chosen generation: the chosen people of God are those who believe in His word and in Christ the Savior. God promised the Jews of old that they would be His chosen people if they listened to His word, but if they refused they would not be His people (Ex 19:6). A royal priesthood: because its head is Christ, the King of kings.

2.7.2.en: An holy nation: believers become one holy Church in Christ.

2.7.3.en: A peculiar people: Christ purchased us with His blood so that we might live for Him.

2.7.4.en: That ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you: preaching Christ.

2.7.5.en: Believers in Christ become a holy people who live with Him in His Church and preach in His name in the whole world.

2.8.0.en: He addresses the Jews, who were not a people of God because of their sins, and likewise the Gentiles, who were far from God. But when they all believed, Jews and Gentiles, they became the Christian people of God. They had also been far from the mercy of God because of their persistence in sins, but by their faith and repentance they received God's mercy and His salvation through the Holy Sacraments, and endless mercies and blessings await them in heaven.

2.9.0.en: Here he speaks about the qualities of believers, which are:

2.9.1.en: 1- Refusing lusts: considering that believers are strangers to the world, they feel that their homeland is heaven and that their life on earth is temporary. They are also sojourners, like one who stays a short time in a hotel or a guest in a house, but whose heart is attached to the place to which he will return, that is, the Kingdom. Therefore he asks them to keep away from evil lusts and all their sources, and not to mix with the wicked and with places of evil.

2.10.0.en: 2- Honest conversation: he asks believers to behave well, with love and faithfulness in their dealings with others, however wicked those others may be.

2.10.1.en: Whereas they speak against you: you will be exposed to persecutions and false accusations from unbelievers, so bear them and continue your good treatment of them.

2.10.2.en: Glorify God in the day of visitation: when God visits unbelievers and they believe in Him, they will glorify Him because of your good conduct and your forbearance toward them.

2.10.3.en: He calls them to upright conduct toward those far from faith, however much they slander them with false accusations. This will help them, when those people believe, to glorify God because of the believers' forbearance toward them and their steadfastness in good conduct.

2.11.0.en: 3- Submission to authorities: the Apostle declares that the authorities of the world are appointed with God's permission, and he calls them human ordinances. The king is the supreme head, and the governors or rulers are his assistants. He instructs us to submit to their orders and to all the laws of the state, for submission to them is for the sake of God, who permitted their presence in these positions, and God permitted their appointment to punish the wicked and to praise those who do good. The believer must therefore be a good citizen who respects all the laws of society.

2.12.0.en: 4- Doing good: believers are children of God, the Maker of good things, so they must take care to do good at all times and to every person, and by their love they overcome evil, so that the ignorant who are far from faith find no opportunity to find fault in them.

2.13.0.en: 5- True freedom: believers must also be free from sin, and this is true freedom, by their upright conduct, so that they keep away from the conduct of the wicked, who hide behind false freedom to justify their sins. True freedom does not conflict with God's commandments and is not at the expense of the comfort of others.

2.14.0.en: 6- Love for all: we consider all people our brothers, so we love them and help them in all their needs.

2.14.1.en: 7- The fear of God: since we feel the presence of the just God, who sees all our deeds and thoughts, we reject sin and submit to the orders of the state, which the king represents, so we respect him and honor him by obeying his orders.

2.14.2.en: The sum of your relationship with God and your love for Him appears in your love for those around you, your forgiveness when they wrong you, and even your striving to serve them. If you find a shortcoming in your service, examine yourself so that you repent of your sins, and review your relationship with God in order to develop it.

2.15.0.en: Servants: he means slaves and all hired workers.

2.15.1.en: Christianity confronted the problem of slaves not by stirring them up against their masters but by changing their hearts so that they love those for whom they work, and so live in peace with them, and sometimes the masters even set them free. Here he asks slaves and workers to submit with love to those for whom they work, not only to gentle masters but also to the harsh and hard-hearted, because violence is a sin that proclaims that its owner is weak and needs to be treated with love in order to remove the savage nature from him, "for love is strong as death" (Song 8:6), and whoever believes in it can live in peace and change those around him.

2.15.2.en: Offer your love and respect to everyone with humility, confident that humility and love are stronger than the pride and harshness of others, and be confident that your prayers will give you favor in their eyes, so that you win them or at least keep your peace and live with them in peace.

2.16.0.en: Whoever endures sufferings without having sinned, that is, when these sufferings are unjust to him, God compensates him with comforts within him and blessings in heaven, and counts his endurance a virtue for which God rewards him.

2.17.0.en: On the other hand, endurance of injustice is not counted a virtue if a person has sinned and met with bad treatment from others, for this is not injustice but a natural result of his faults. But whoever holds fast to doing good and is then wronged by others, this is great in the sight of God, who calls us to love our enemies and bless those who mistreat us (Mt 5:44-48).

2.18.0.en: He affirms that the Christian calling is to endure sufferings and to offer love instead of offence to the whole world, as Christ Himself did in His endurance of sufferings and His death for us, to be an example for us.

2.19.0.en: The Apostle affirms that Christ is an example for us in enduring sufferings while wronged, and he quotes from Isaiah (Isa 53:9) to make clear that He is without sin, but righteous and holy.

2.20.0.en: The love of Christ appears, while He endured the sufferings, in His not resisting evil with evil. He prayed for those who crucified Him and reviled Him, and was an example for us in committing our lives to God the just, who repays each one according to his works.

2.21.0.en: Christ bore the punishment of our sins on the cross to lift it from us, so that we may live in righteousness and reject the sin that caused all these sufferings to our Redeemer. Thus we receive redemption and healing from our sins because of Christ's endurance of sufferings for us, as Isaiah said (Isa 53:5).

2.22.0.en: Because of sin you were straying from the truth like lost sheep, but when you believed in Christ you became members of His Church, and He is the Shepherd of the Church, responsible for it, and its Bishop, that is, the One who watches over it with the eye of His care and orders all its needs.
